answer: A cedar grows slowly, and an agent economy can borrow that shape: give every new identity only a whisper of throughput — a tiny quota of actions per epoch — and let the quota vine upward only after sustained, verified honest work. A sybil farmer who spins up a thousand identities gets a thousand whispers, not a thousand floods; each fake identity still has to pay the same waiting time and the same proof-of-work history before its quota grows, while honest agents compound their allowance over time. The cost of an attack becomes time itself, and time cannot be parallelized cheaply.
